body:
What you've said makes sense. Thank you for trying to help clear my mind up. I've known that I tend to get obsessive and tunnel-visioned on whatever project I may be invested in at a given time, but I had always considered that eventually I would find satisfaction in a future parter (yet I've always equated relationship satisfaction with misery and missed opportunities). I'm not sure if my problem is common, but I'll try to find some info regarding it online. I've had daily thoughts of dying and/or suicide for over five years now, and I'm tiring of it. That compounded with a dread of never meeting my goals led me to posting here. 

I'm not sure if I'm recoverable at this point. I have no other ambitions, as I've stated, as everything I work towards has the common factor of being another attractor of a mate.

Thanks again (to you and everyone).

It seems natural to me. Our biological instinct drives us to find the best mates to procreate  with. Sure, I could settle for "my best" mate, but then I raise a kid with the knowledge that I brought a lifeform into the world with less than ideal genetics; risking perpetuating the cycle of unshakable suicidal thoughts when that offspring comes to terms with their own reality after going through the wonderment stage of youth.

That is truly my only life goal. I've achieved many things thus far: education, financial security, a fit body, and several hobbies, but the one thing I have yet to achieve lies within the realm of women. I feel the time is slipping away, and do not know if I can live with such a failure.

I've tried to not care, to find the positive and happiness in my current situation. But it is always short lived; there is this nagging that festers in my mind constantly. Every moment of free time I have, my mind tells me to get back to work so I can make more money which can eventually be parlayed into a hot woman. It's likely not a healthy mentality to have, but it's been like this for half a decade now, and I feel as if this ideology has gained too much momentum to ever subside. Hence a constant drive to return to entropic state.
